# googlesheets

## GOOGLESHEETS_ADD_SHEET
Adds a new sheet to a spreadsheet. Supports three sheet types: GRID, OBJECT, and DATA_SOURCE. SHEET TYPES: - GRID (default): Standard spreadsheet with rows/columns. Use properties to set dimensions, tab color, etc. - OBJECT: Sheet containing a chart. Requires objectSheetConfig with chartSpec (basicChart or pieChart). - DATA_SOURCE: Sheet connected to BigQuery. Requires dataSourceConfig with bigQuery spec and bigquery.readonly OAuth scope. OTHER NOTES: - Sheet names must be unique; use forceUnique=true to auto-append suffix (_2, _3) if name exists - For tab colors, use EITHER rgbColor OR themeColor, not both - Avoid 'index' when creating sheets in parallel (causes errors) - OBJECT sheets are created via addChart with position.newSheet=true - DATA_SOURCE sheets require bigquery.readonly OAuth scope Use cases: Add standard grid sheet, create chart on dedicated sheet, connect to BigQuery data source.

## GOOGLESHEETS_AGGREGATE_COLUMN_DATA
Searches for rows where a specific column matches a value and performs mathematical operations on data from another column.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "AggregateColumnDataRequest",
  "required": [
    "spreadsheet_id",
    "sheet_name",
    "target_column",
    "operation"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "operation": {
      "enum": [
        "sum",
        "average",
        "count",
        "min",
        "max",
        "percentage"
      ],
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Operation",
      "examples": [
        "sum",
        "average",
        "count",
        "min",
        "max",
        "percentage"
      ],
      "description": "The mathematical operation to perform on the target column values.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Operation",
      "human_parameter_description": "Select the type of calculation you want to perform on the values from the target column."
    },
    "sheet_name": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Sheet Name",
      "examples": [
        "Sheet1",
        "Sales Data"
      ],
      "description": "The name of the specific sheet within the spreadsheet. Matching is case-insensitive. If no exact match is found, partial matches will be attempted (e.g., 'overview' will match 'Overview 2025').",
      "human_parameter_name": "Sheet Name",
      "human_parameter_description": "Specify which sheet in the spreadsheet you want to use for your data aggregation. Matching is case-insensitive and supports partial matches."
    },
    "search_value": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Search Value",
      "examples": [
        "HSR",
        "Sales",
        "North Region"
      ],
      "description": "The exact value to search for in the search column. Case-sensitive by default. If not provided (or if search_column is not provided), all rows in the target column will be aggregated without filtering.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Search Value",
      "human_parameter_description": "Provide the specific value you want to find in the selected search column. Leave empty to aggregate all rows."
    },
    "search_column": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Search Column",
      "examples": [
        "A",
        "Region",
        "Department"
      ],
      "description": "The column to search in for filtering rows. Can be a letter (e.g., 'A', 'B') or column name from header row (e.g., 'Region', 'Department'). If not provided, all rows in the target column will be aggregated without filtering.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Search Column",
      "human_parameter_description": "Indicate the column you want to look through to find matching values. Leave empty to aggregate all rows."
    },
    "target_column": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Target Column",
      "examples": [
        "D",
        "Sales",
        "Revenue"
      ],
      "description": "The column to aggregate data from. Can be a letter (e.g., 'C', 'D') or column name from header row (e.g., 'Sales', 'Revenue').",
      "human_parameter_name": "Target Column",
      "human_parameter_description": "This is the column from which you want to gather and perform calculations on data."
    },
    "case_sensitive": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Case Sensitive",
      "default": true,
      "examples": [
        true,
        false
      ],
      "description": "Whether the search should be case-sensitive.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Case Sensitive",
      "human_parameter_description": "Decide if the search should match upper and lower case letters exactly."
    },
    "has_header_row": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Has Header Row",
      "default": true,
      "examples": [
        true,
        false
      ],
      "description": "Whether the first row contains column headers. If True, column names can be used for search_column and target_column.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Has Header Row",
      "human_parameter_description": "Indicate if your data has column names in the first row, which helps in identifying columns by name."
    },
    "spreadsheet_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Spreadsheet Id",
      "examples": [
        "1BxiMVs0XRA5nFMdKvBdBZjgmUUqptlbs74OgvE2upms"
      ],
      "description": "The unique identifier of the Google Sheets spreadsheet.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Spreadsheet Id",
      "human_parameter_description": "The unique ID for locating the specific spreadsheet you want to work with."
    },
    "percentage_total": {
      "type": "number",
      "title": "Percentage Total",
      "examples": [
        10000,
        50000.5
      ],
      "description": "For percentage operation, the total value to calculate percentage against. If not provided, uses sum of all values in target column.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Percentage Total",
      "human_parameter_description": "If you're calculating a percentage, this is the total value to compare against. If you leave this blank, it will use the total of the target column."
    },
    "additional_filters": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "object",
        "title": "AdditionalFilter",
        "required": [
          "column",
          "value"
        ],
        "properties": {
          "value": {
            "type": "string",
            "title": "Value",
            "examples": [
              "APAC",
              "Beacon",
              "North"
            ],
            "description": "Exact value to match in the column."
          },
          "column": {
            "type": "string",
            "title": "Column",
            "examples": [
              "Region",
              "B",
              "Product"
            ],
            "description": "Column letter (e.g., 'B') or header name (e.g., 'Region') to filter on."
          }
        },
        "description": "An extra column=value filter applied with AND logic on top of search_column/search_value."
      },
      "title": "Additional Filters",
      "description": "Extra column=value conditions applied with AND logic on top of search_column/search_value. Use this to filter on multiple columns simultaneously. Example: [{\"column\": \"Region\", \"value\": \"APAC\"}] combined with search_column=Product/search_value=Beacon returns only rows where Product=Beacon AND Region=APAC.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Additional Filters",
      "human_parameter_description": "Add extra column filters (AND logic) to narrow down which rows are included in the aggregation. Each filter specifies a column and the exact value it must contain."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request to search for rows matching a column value and aggregate data from another column."
}

## GOOGLESHEETS_APPEND_DIMENSION
Tool to append new rows or columns to a sheet, increasing its size. Use when you need to add empty rows or columns to an existing sheet.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "AppendDimensionRequest",
  "required": [
    "spreadsheet_id",
    "sheet_id",
    "dimension",
    "length"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "length": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Length",
      "examples": [
        10
      ],
      "description": "The number of rows or columns to append.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Length",
      "human_parameter_description": "Specify how many new rows or columns you want to add to the sheet."
    },
    "sheet_id": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Sheet Id",
      "examples": [
        0
      ],
      "description": "The numeric ID of the sheet (not the sheet name). This is a non-negative integer found in the sheet's URL as the 'gid' parameter (e.g., gid=0) or in the sheet properties. The first sheet in a spreadsheet typically has sheet_id=0.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Sheet ID",
      "human_parameter_description": "Provide the numeric sheet ID (not the sheet name). Find it in the URL 'gid' parameter or use GOOGLESHEETS_GET_SHEET_NAMES to retrieve sheet IDs. The first sheet typically has ID 0."
    },
    "dimension": {
      "enum": [
        "ROWS",
        "COLUMNS"
      ],
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Dimension",
      "examples": [
        "ROWS"
      ],
      "description": "Specifies whether to append rows or columns.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Dimension Type",
      "human_parameter_description": "Indicate whether you want to append rows or columns to the sheet."
    },
    "spreadsheet_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Spreadsheet Id",
      "examples": [
        "1q2w3e4r5t6y7u8i9o0p"
      ],
      "description": "The ID of the spreadsheet.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Spreadsheet Id",
      "human_parameter_description": "The ID of the spreadsheet."
    },
    "response_ranges": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "title": "Response Ranges",
      "description": "Limits the ranges of the spreadsheet to include in the response.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Response Ranges",
      "human_parameter_description": "Limit the response to only include data from specific ranges in the spreadsheet."
    },
    "response_include_grid_data": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Response Include Grid Data",
      "description": "True if grid data should be included in the response (if includeSpreadsheetInResponse is true).",
      "human_parameter_name": "Include Grid Data?",
      "human_parameter_description": "Set to true to include the actual cell data in the response when includeSpreadsheetInResponse is also true."
    },
    "include_spreadsheet_in_response": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Include Spreadsheet In Response",
      "description": "True if the updated spreadsheet should be included in the response.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Include Spreadsheet in Response?",
      "human_parameter_description": "Set to true if you want the full updated spreadsheet data returned in the response."
    }
  }
}

## GOOGLESHEETS_AUTO_RESIZE_DIMENSIONS
Auto-fit column widths or row heights for a dimension range using batchUpdate.autoResizeDimensions. Use when you need to automatically adjust row heights or column widths to fit content after writing data.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "AutoResizeDimensionsRequest",
  "required": [
    "spreadsheet_id",
    "dimension",
    "start_index",
    "end_index"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "sheet_id": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Sheet Id",
      "examples": [
        0,
        123456789
      ],
      "description": "The numeric ID of the sheet to resize. Either sheet_id or sheet_name must be provided. If both are provided, sheet_name takes precedence and will be resolved to sheet_id."
    },
    "dimension": {
      "enum": [
        "ROWS",
        "COLUMNS"
      ],
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Dimension",
      "examples": [
        "COLUMNS",
        "ROWS"
      ],
      "description": "The dimension to auto-resize. Use 'ROWS' to auto-fit row heights or 'COLUMNS' to auto-fit column widths."
    },
    "end_index": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "End Index",
      "minimum": 1,
      "examples": [
        3,
        10
      ],
      "description": "The zero-based end index of the dimension range to resize (exclusive). Must be greater than start_index. For example, to resize columns A-C, use start_index=0 and end_index=3."
    },
    "sheet_name": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Sheet Name",
      "examples": [
        "Sheet1",
        "Sales Data"
      ],
      "description": "The name of the sheet to resize. Either sheet_id or sheet_name must be provided. Using sheet_name is recommended as it's more intuitive. If both sheet_id and sheet_name are provided, sheet_name takes precedence."
    },
    "start_index": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Start Index",
      "minimum": 0,
      "examples": [
        0,
        5
      ],
      "description": "The zero-based start index of the dimension range to resize (inclusive). For columns, 0 = column A. For rows, 0 = row 1."
    },
    "spreadsheet_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Spreadsheet Id",
      "examples": [
        "1BxiMVs0XRA5nFMdKvBdBZjgmUUqptlbs74OgvE2upms"
      ],
      "description": "The ID of the spreadsheet containing the sheet to resize."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request model for auto-resizing dimensions (rows or columns) in a Google Sheet."
}
```

      },

    }

## GOOGLESHEETS_BATCH_CLEAR_VALUES_BY_DATA_FILTER
Clears one or more ranges of values from a spreadsheet using data filters. The caller must specify the spreadsheet ID and one or more DataFilters. Ranges matching any of the specified data filters will be cleared. Only values are cleared -- all other properties of the cell (such as formatting, data validation, etc..) are kept.

Retrieves data from specified cell ranges in a Google Spreadsheet.

**Input schema:**

{

      ],
      "description": "A list of cell ranges in A1 notation from which to retrieve data. Supported formats: (1) Bare sheet name like 'Sheet1' to get all data from that sheet, (2) Sheet with range like 'Sheet1!A1:B2', (3) Just cell reference like 'A1:B2' (uses first sheet). For sheet names with spaces or special characters, enclose in single quotes (e.g., \"'My Sheet'\" or \"'My Sheet'!A1:B2\"). IMPORTANT: For large sheets, always use bounded ranges with explicit row limits (e.g., 'Sheet1!A1:Z10000' instead of 'Sheet1!A:Z'). ## GOOGLESHEETS_BATCH_UPDATE
DEPRECATED: Use GOOGLESHEETS_VALUES_UPDATE instead. Write values to ONE range in a Google Sheet, or append as new rows if no start cell is given. IMPORTANT - This tool does NOT accept the Google Sheets API's native batch format: - WRONG: {"data": [{"range": "...", "values": [[...]]}], ...} - CORRECT: {"sheet_name": "...", "values": [[...]], "first_cell_location": "...", ...} To update MULTIPLE ranges, make SEPARATE CALLS to this tool for each range. Features: - Auto-expands grid for large datasets (prevents range errors) - Set first_cell_location to write at a specific position (e.g., "A1", "B5") - Omit first_cell_location to append values as new rows at the end Requirements: Target sheet must exist and spreadsheet must contain at least one worksheet.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "BatchUpdateRequest",

    "spreadsheet_id",
    "sheet_name",

    },

      "type": "string",
      "title": "Sheet Name",
      "examples": [
        "Sheet1",
        "Sales Data",

      ],

Case-insensitive matching is supported (e.g., 'sheet1' will match 'Sheet1'). If you specify a common default name like 'Sheet1' and it doesn't exist, the action will automatically use the first sheet in the spreadsheet.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Sheet Name",
      "human_parameter_description": "Provide the name of the sheet you want to update. Case-insensitive matching is supported, so 'sheet1' will match 'Sheet1'."

      "title": "Spreadsheet Id",
      "examples": [

## GOOGLESHEETS_CLEAR_BASIC_FILTER
Tool to clear the basic filter from a sheet. Use when you need to remove an existing basic filter from a specific sheet within a Google Spreadsheet.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ClearBasicFilterRequest",
  "required": [
    "spreadsheet_id",
    "sheet_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "sheet_id": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Sheet Id",
      "examples": [
        0,
        123456789
      ],
      "description": "The ID of the sheet on which the basic filter should be cleared.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Sheet ID",
      "human_parameter_description": "Specify the ID of the sheet from which you want to remove the basic filter."
    },
    "spreadsheet_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Spreadsheet Id",
      "examples": [
        "abc123xyz789"
      ],
      "description": "The ID of the spreadsheet.",

      "human_parameter_description": "Provide the unique identifier for the spreadsheet you want to modify."
    },
    "response_ranges": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "title": "Response Ranges",
      "description": "Limits the ranges included in the response spreadsheet. Only applicable when include_spreadsheet_in_response is true.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Response Ranges",
      "human_parameter_description": "List of A1 notation ranges to include in the response (e.g., ['Sheet1!A1:D5'])."

    "response_include_grid_data": {

    }
  }
}

## GOOGLESHEETS_CLEAR_VALUES
Clears cell content (preserving formatting and notes) from a specified A1 notation range in a Google Spreadsheet; the range must correspond to an existing sheet and cells.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ClearValuesRequest",
  "required": [
    "spreadsheet_id",
    "range"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "range": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Range",
      "examples": [
        "Sheet1!A1:B10",
        "Sheet2!C:D",
        "A1:Z100",
        "My Custom Sheet!B3:F10"
      ],
      "description": "The A1 notation of the range to clear values from (e.g., 'Sheet1!A1:B2', 'MySheet!C:C', or 'A1:D5'). If the sheet name is omitted (e.g., 'A1:B2'), the operation applies to the first visible sheet.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Range",
      "human_parameter_description": "Specify the range of cells you want to clear using A1 notation. This helps define exactly which cells will be affected in the spreadsheet."
    },
    "spreadsheet_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Spreadsheet Id",
      "examples": [
        "1qZ_g6N0g3Z0s5hJ2xQ8vP9r7T_u6X3iY2o0kE_l5N7M",
        "spre\u03b1dsheetId_from_url"
      ],
      "description": "The unique identifier of the Google Spreadsheet from which to clear values. This ID can be found in the URL of the spreadsheet.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Spreadsheet ID",
      "human_parameter_description": "Provide the unique ID of the Google Spreadsheet where you want to clear data. You can find this ID in the spreadsheet's URL."
    }
  }
}
```

**Output schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "$defs": {

If an unbounded or oversized range was requested, this reports the actual cleared range constrained by the sheet's limits. Sheet names with spaces or special characters are quoted (e.g., Sheet1!A1:C10, 'My Sheet'!B2:B100, or 'Tab Name'!A12)."

Sheet names with spaces or special characters are quoted (e.g., Sheet1!A1:C10, 'My Sheet'!B2:B100, or 'Tab Name'!A12)."

## GOOGLESHEETS_CREATE_CHART
Create a chart in a Google Sheets spreadsheet using the specified data range and chart type. Conditional requirements: - Provide either a simple chart via chart_type + data_range (basicChart), OR supply a full chart_spec supporting all chart types. Exactly one approach should be used. - When using chart_spec, set exactly one of the union fields (basicChart | pieChart | bubbleChart | candlestickChart | histogramChart | waterfallChart | treemapChart | orgChart | scorecardChart).

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "CreateChartRequest",
  "required": [
    "spreadsheet_id",
    "sheet_id",
    "chart_type",
    "data_range"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "title": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Title",
      "examples": [
        "Sales Data",
        "Monthly Revenue"
      ],
      "description": "Optional title for the chart.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Chart Title",
      "human_parameter_description": "Provide a title for the chart to give context to viewers."
    },
    "sheet_id": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Sheet Id",
      "examples": [
        0,
        123456789
      ],
      "description": "The numeric sheetId (not the sheet name/title) of the worksheet where the chart will be created. This is a unique integer identifier for the sheet within the spreadsheet. The first/default sheet typically has sheetId=0. IMPORTANT: Use 'Get Spreadsheet Info' action to retrieve valid sheetIds - look for sheets[].properties.sheetId in the response. The sheetId must exist in the target spreadsheet; using an ID from a different spreadsheet will fail.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Sheet ID",
      "human_parameter_description": "Enter the numeric ID of the worksheet within the spreadsheet where the chart is to be placed. Use Get Spreadsheet Info to find valid sheet IDs."
    },
    "subtitle": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Subtitle",
      "examples": [
        "Q1 2024",
        "Year over Year"
      ],
      "description": "Optional subtitle for the chart.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Chart Subtitle",
      "human_parameter_description": "Add a subtitle to provide additional context for the chart."
    },
    "chart_spec": {
      "type": "object",
      "title": "Chart Spec",
      "examples": [
        {
          "pieChart": {
            "domain": {
              "sourceRange": {
                "sources": [
                  {
                    "sheetId": 0,
                    "endRowIndex": 5,
                    "startRowIndex": 0,
                    "endColumnIndex": 1,
                    "startColumnIndex": 0
                  }
                ]
              }
            },
            "series": {
              "sourceRange": {
                "sources": [
                  {
                    "sheetId": 0,
                    "endRowIndex": 5,
                    "startRowIndex": 0,
                    "endColumnIndex": 2,
                    "startColumnIndex": 1
                  }
                ]
              }
            },
            "legendPosition": "RIGHT_LEGEND"
          }
        }
      ],
      "description": "Optional full ChartSpec object to send to the Google Sheets API. Use this to support ALL chart types and advanced options. Must set exactly one of: basicChart, pieChart, bubbleChart, candlestickChart, histogramChart, treemapChart, waterfallChart, orgChart, scorecardChart. See https://developers.google.com/workspace/sheets/api/reference/rest/v4/spreadsheets/charts#ChartSpec.",
      "additionalProperties": true,
      "human_parameter_name": "Chart Spec",
      "human_parameter_description": "Optionally, provide a detailed chart specification for more advanced charting options."
    },
    "chart_type": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Chart Type",
      "examples": [
        "COLUMN",
        "LINE",
        "BAR",
        "AREA",
        "PIE",
        "SCATTER",
        "COMBO"
      ],
      "description": "The type of chart to create. Case-insensitive. Supported types: BAR, LINE, AREA, COLUMN, SCATTER, COMBO, STEPPED_AREA (basic charts with axes), PIE (pie/donut charts), HISTOGRAM, BUBBLE, CANDLESTICK (requires 4+ data columns for low/open/close/high), TREEMAP, WATERFALL, ORG (organizational charts), SCORECARD. Each chart type uses its appropriate Google Sheets API spec structure. For advanced customization, provide chart_spec instead.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Chart Type",
      "human_parameter_description": "Specify the type of chart you want to create from the available options."
    },
    "data_range": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Data Range",
      "examples": [
        "A1:C10",
        "Sheet1!B2:D20",
        "Data!A1:E50"
      ],
      "description": "A single contiguous range of data for the chart in A1 notation (e.g., 'A1:C10' or 'Sheet1!B2:D20'). Must be a single continuous range - comma-separated multi-ranges (e.g., 'A1:A10,C1:C10') are not supported. When chart_spec is not provided, the first column is used as the domain/labels and the remaining columns as series. IMPORTANT: PIE charts require at least 2 columns - the first column for category labels (domain) and the second column for numeric values (series). Single-column ranges are not supported for PIE charts.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Data Range",
      "human_parameter_description": "Provide the range of data you want to include in the chart using A1 notation."
    },
    "x_axis_title": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "X Axis Title",
      "examples": [
        "Time Period",
        "Categories"

## GOOGLESHEETS_CREATE_GOOGLE_SHEET1
Creates a new Google Spreadsheet in Google Drive. If a title is provided, the spreadsheet will be created with that name. If no title is provided, Google will create a spreadsheet with a default name like 'Untitled spreadsheet'.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "CreateGoogleSheetRequest",
  "properties": {
    "title": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Title",
      "examples": [
        "Q4 Financial Report",
        "Project Plan Ideas",
        "Meeting Notes"
      ],
      "description": "The title for the new Google Sheet. If omitted, Google will create a spreadsheet with a default name like 'Untitled spreadsheet'.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Title",
      "human_parameter_description": "The title for the new Google Sheet. If omitted, Google will create a spreadsheet with a default name like 'Untitled spreadsheet'."
    }
  }
}
```

**Output schema:**

  "$defs": {

      "title": "Sheet",
      "properties": {
        "properties": {

          "title": "Properties",
          "properties": {

## GOOGLESHEETS_CREATE_SPREADSHEET_COLUMN
Creates a new column in a Google Spreadsheet. Specify the target sheet using sheet_id (numeric) or sheet_name (text). If neither is provided, defaults to the first sheet (sheet_id=0).

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "CreateSpreadsheetColumnRequest",
  "required": [
    "spreadsheet_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "sheet_id": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Sheet Id",
      "examples": [
        0,
        123456789
      ],
      "description": "The numeric identifier of the specific sheet (tab) within the spreadsheet. Defaults to 0 (the first sheet) if neither sheet_id nor sheet_name is provided. Use GOOGLESHEETS_GET_SHEET_NAMES or GOOGLESHEETS_FIND_WORKSHEET_BY_TITLE to obtain the sheet_id from a sheet name.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Sheet ID",
      "human_parameter_description": "Enter the numeric ID of the sheet where you wish to add the column. The first sheet usually has ID 0."
    },
    "sheet_name": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Sheet Name",
      "examples": [
        "Sheet1",
        "Data",
        "Q1 Report"
      ],
      "description": "The name (title) of the sheet/tab where the column will be added. If provided, the action will look up the sheet_id automatically. If both sheet_id and sheet_name are provided, sheet_id takes precedence.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Sheet Name",
      "human_parameter_description": "Enter the name of the sheet/tab where you want to add the column. This is an alternative to specifying sheet_id."
    },
    "insert_index": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Insert Index",
      "default": 0,
      "examples": [
        0,
        1,
        5
      ],
      "description": "The 0-based index at which the new column will be inserted. For example, an index of 0 inserts the column before the current first column (A), and an index of 1 inserts it between the current columns A and B.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Insert Index",
      "human_parameter_description": "Specify the position where the new column should be added, counting from the left."
    },
    "spreadsheet_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Spreadsheet Id",
      "examples": [
        "1qZysYd_N2cZ9gkZ8sR7M0rP8sX5vW2bA9gV3rF1cE0"
      ],
      "description": "The unique identifier of the Google Spreadsheet where the column will be created.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Spreadsheet ID",
      "human_parameter_description": "Provide the unique ID of the Google Spreadsheet where you want to add the new column."
    },
    "response_ranges": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "title": "Response Ranges",
      "examples": [
        [
          "Sheet1!A1:D10"
        ],
        [
          "A1:B5",
          "C1:D10"
        ]
      ],
      "description": "Limits the ranges of the spreadsheet to include in the response. Only used if includeSpreadsheetInResponse is true.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Response Ranges",
      "human_parameter_description": "Limit the response to only include data from specific ranges in the spreadsheet."
    },
    "inherit_from_before": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Inherit From Before",
      "default": false,
      "examples": [
        true,
        false
      ],
      "description": "If true, the new column inherits properties (e.g., formatting, width) from the column immediately to its left (the preceding column). If false (default), it inherits from the column immediately to its right (the succeeding column). This is ignored if there is no respective preceding or succeeding column.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Inherit from Before?",
      "human_parameter_description": "Decide if the new column should copy properties from the column on its left."
    },
    "response_include_grid_data": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Response Include Grid Data",
      "examples": [
        true,
        false
      ],
      "description": "If true, grid data will be included in the response (only used if includeSpreadsheetInResponse is true).",
      "human_parameter_name": "Include Grid Data?",
      "human_parameter_description": "Set to true to include the actual cell data in the response when includeSpreadsheetInResponse is also true."
    },
    "include_spreadsheet_in_response": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Include Spreadsheet In Response",
      "examples": [
        true,
        false
      ],
      "description": "If true, the updated spreadsheet will be included in the response. Defaults to true if not specified.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Include Spreadsheet in Response?",
      "human_parameter_description": "Set to true if you want the full updated spreadsheet data returned in the response."
    }
  }
}
```

## GOOGLESHEETS_CREATE_SPREADSHEET_ROW
Inserts a new, empty row into a specified sheet of a Google Spreadsheet at a given index, optionally inheriting formatting from the row above.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "CreateSpreadsheetRowRequest",
  "required": [
    "spreadsheet_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "sheet_id": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Sheet Id",
      "examples": [
        0,
        123456789
      ],
      "description": "The numeric identifier of the sheet (tab) within the spreadsheet where the row will be inserted. This ID (gid) is found in the URL of the spreadsheet (e.g., '0' for the first sheet). Either sheet_id or sheet_name must be provided.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Sheet ID",
      "human_parameter_description": "Specify the sheet ID where you want to insert the row. This is usually found in the URL and pertains to the specific tab in your spreadsheet."
    },
    "sheet_name": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Sheet Name",
      "examples": [
        "Sheet1",
        "Data",
        "Q3 Report"
      ],
      "description": "The human-readable name of the sheet (tab) within the spreadsheet where the row will be inserted (e.g., 'Sheet1'). Either sheet_id or sheet_name must be provided. If both are provided, sheet_id takes precedence.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Sheet Name",
      "human_parameter_description": "Specify the sheet name (tab title) where you want to insert the row, such as 'Sheet1'."
    },
    "insert_index": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Insert Index",
      "default": 0,
      "examples": [
        0,
        5,
        100
      ],
      "description": "The 0-based index at which the new row should be inserted. For example, an index of 0 inserts the row at the beginning of the sheet. If the index is greater than the current number of rows, the row is appended.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Insert Index",
      "human_parameter_description": "Indicate the position where the new row should go. For example, use 0 to place it at the top, or any index number to insert it elsewhere."
    },
    "spreadsheet_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Spreadsheet Id",
      "examples": [
        "1qpyC0XzHc_-_d824s2VfopkHh7D0jW4aXCS1D_AlGA"
      ],
      "description": "The unique identifier of the Google Spreadsheet. Can be provided as the ID (e.g., '1qpyC0XzHc_-_d824s2VfopkHh7D0jW4aXCS1D_AlGA') or as a full URL (the ID will be extracted automatically).",
      "human_parameter_name": "Spreadsheet ID",
      "human_parameter_description": "Provide the ID of the Google Spreadsheet where you want to add a new row. You can find it in the spreadsheet's URL, or paste the full URL and the ID will be extracted automatically."
    },
    "response_ranges": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "title": "Response Ranges",
      "examples": [
        [
          "Sheet1!A1:D10"
        ],
        [
          "Sheet1!A:A",
          "Sheet2!B:B"
        ]
      ],
      "description": "Limits the ranges included in the response spreadsheet. Only meaningful when include_spreadsheet_in_response is True. Use A1 notation (e.g., ['Sheet1!A1:D10']).",
      "human_parameter_name": "Response Ranges",
      "human_parameter_description": "Optionally limit the response to specific ranges of the spreadsheet. Only applies when include_spreadsheet_in_response is True."
    },
    "inherit_from_before": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Inherit From Before",
      "default": false,
      "examples": [
        true,
        false
      ],
      "description": "If True, the newly inserted row will inherit formatting and properties from the row immediately preceding its insertion point. If False, it will have default formatting.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Inherit formatting from previous row?",
      "human_parameter_description": "Decide if the new row should take on the style of the row right before it. Choose 'Yes' to carry over formatting, or 'No' for a default look."
    },
    "response_include_grid_data": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Response Include Grid Data",
      "examples": [
        true,
        false
      ],
      "description": "If True, grid data will be included in the response spreadsheet. Only meaningful when include_spreadsheet_in_response is True. Default is False.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Include Grid Data in Response?",
      "human_parameter_description": "Choose whether to include the actual cell data in the response. Only applies when include_spreadsheet_in_response is True."
    },
    "include_spreadsheet_in_response": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Include Spreadsheet In Response",
      "examples": [
        true,
        false
      ],
      "description": "If True, the response will include the full updated Spreadsheet resource. Default behavior includes the spreadsheet when this parameter is not specified.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Include Spreadsheet in Response?",
      "human_parameter_description": "Choose whether to include the full updated spreadsheet data in the response. Useful for getting the complete spreadsheet state after the update."
    }
  }
}

            "type": "object",

          },

          "description": "Per-request replies corresponding 1:1 with the requests; replies to some requests may be empty. For InsertDimensionRequest (row insertion), the reply object is empty."

          "description": "The URL to view the spreadsheet in Google Sheets."

          "properties": {
            "sheets": {
              "type": "array",
              "items": {
                "type": "object",

## GOOGLESHEETS_DELETE_DIMENSION
Tool to delete specified rows or columns from a sheet in a Google Spreadsheet. Use when you need to remove a range of rows or columns.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "DeleteDimensionRequest",
  "required": [
    "spreadsheet_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "sheet_id": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Sheet Id",
      "examples": [
        0,
        123456789
      ],
      "description": "The unique numeric ID of the sheet (not the index/position). This ID is assigned by Google Sheets and does not change when sheets are reordered. Use GOOGLESHEETS_GET_SPREADSHEET_INFO to find the sheet ID, or use sheet_name instead. Either sheet_id or sheet_name must be provided."
    },
    "dimension": {
      "enum": [
        "ROWS",
        "COLUMNS"
      ],
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Dimension",
      "examples": [
        "ROWS",
        "COLUMNS"
      ],
      "description": "The dimension to delete (ROWS or COLUMNS)."
    },
    "end_index": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "End Index",
      "examples": [
        1,
        10
      ],
      "description": "The zero-based end index of the range to delete, exclusive. Must be greater than start_index and at most equal to the sheet's current row/column count. Note: Cannot delete all rows or columns from a sheet - at least one row and one column must remain."
    },
    "sheet_name": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Sheet Name",
      "examples": [
        "Sheet1",
        "MySheet"
      ],
      "description": "The name/title of the sheet from which to delete the dimension. Using sheet_name is recommended as it's more intuitive than sheet_id. Either sheet_id or sheet_name must be provided."

      "title": "Start Index",
      "examples": [
        0,
        5
      ],

      "type": "string",
      "title": "Spreadsheet Id",

              ],

## GOOGLESHEETS_DELETE_SHEET
Tool to delete a sheet (worksheet) from a spreadsheet. Use when you need to remove a specific sheet from a Google Sheet document.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "DeleteSheetRequest",
  "required": [
    "spreadsheetId",
    "sheetId"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "sheetId": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Sheet Id",
      "examples": [
        123456789
      ],
      "description": "The ID of the sheet to delete. Note: A spreadsheet must contain at least one sheet, so you cannot delete the last remaining sheet. If the sheet is of DATA_SOURCE type, the associated DataSource is also deleted.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Sheet ID",
      "human_parameter_description": "Enter the ID of the specific sheet you wish to remove from the spreadsheet."
    },
    "spreadsheetId": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Spreadsheet Id",
      "examples": [
        "abc123xyz789"
      ],
      "description": "The ID of the spreadsheet from which to delete the sheet.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Spreadsheet ID",
      "human_parameter_description": "Provide the unique identifier of the spreadsheet that contains the sheet you want to delete."
    },
    "responseRanges": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "title": "Response Ranges",
      "examples": [
        [
          "Sheet1!A1:B10",
          "Sheet2!C1:D20"
        ]
      ],
      "description": "Limits which ranges are returned when includeSpreadsheetInResponse is true. Only meaningful if includeSpreadsheetInResponse is set to true. Ranges should be in A1 notation (e.g., 'Sheet1!A1:B10').",
      "human_parameter_name": "Response Ranges",
      "human_parameter_description": "Specify which ranges to include in the response spreadsheet (requires includeSpreadsheetInResponse=true)."
    },
    "responseIncludeGridData": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Response Include Grid Data",
      "description": "True if grid data should be returned in the response spreadsheet. Only meaningful when includeSpreadsheetInResponse is true and no field mask is set on the request.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Response Include Grid Data",
      "human_parameter_description": "Set to true to include cell data in the response (requires includeSpreadsheetInResponse=true)."
    },
    "includeSpreadsheetInResponse": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Include Spreadsheet In Response",
      "description": "Determines if the spreadsheet resource should be returned in the response. If true, the response includes the updated spreadsheet resource with all its sheets, properties, and metadata.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Include Spreadsheet In Response",
      "human_parameter_description": "Set to true to receive the complete updated spreadsheet in the response."
    }
  }
}

## GOOGLESHEETS_EXECUTE_SQL
DEPRECATED: Use direct Google Sheets actions instead: - GOOGLESHEETS_VALUES_GET / GOOGLESHEETS_BATCH_GET for reads - GOOGLESHEETS_VALUES_UPDATE / GOOGLESHEETS_UPDATE_VALUES_BATCH / GOOGLESHEETS_SPREADSHEETS_VALUES_APPEND for writes Execute SQL queries against Google Sheets tables. Supports SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE operations and WITH clauses (CTEs) with familiar SQL syntax. Tables are automatically detected and mapped from the spreadsheet structure.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ExecuteSqlRequest",
  "required": [
    "spreadsheet_id",
    "sql"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "sql": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Sql",
      "examples": [
        "SELECT * FROM \"Sales_Data\" LIMIT 10",
        "WITH ActiveUsers AS (SELECT * FROM \"Users\" WHERE status = 'active') SELECT name, email FROM ActiveUsers",
        "INSERT INTO \"Customers\" (name, email) VALUES ('John Doe', 'john@example.com')",
        "UPDATE \"Inventory\" SET quantity = quantity - 10 WHERE sku = 'ABC123'",
        "DELETE FROM \"Old_Data\" WHERE date < '2023-01-01'"
      ],
      "description": "Complete SQL query to execute. Must begin with SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, or WITH. Supports Common Table Expressions (CTEs) using WITH clause for complex queries. Note: WITH clauses require the sqlglot library for full support; simple SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE operations work without it. Use table names (sheet names) in FROM/INTO clauses, not A1 range notation. The query must include proper SQL clauses (e.g., SELECT columns FROM table, not just a column name or condition). Example: SELECT * FROM \"Sheet1\" WHERE A = 'value' (correct) instead of just A = 'value' (incorrect).",
      "human_parameter_name": "SQL query",
      "human_parameter_description": "Enter the SQL command you wish to execute on the spreadsheet. This allows you to manipulate data directly using familiar SQL syntax."
    },
    "dry_run": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Dry Run",
      "default": false,
      "description": "Preview changes without applying them (for write operations)",
      "human_parameter_name": "Preview changes?",
      "human_parameter_description": "Select this option if you want to see what changes would be made without actually applying them. It's a safe way to check before executing."
    },
    "delete_method": {
      "enum": [
        "clear",
        "remove_rows"
      ],
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Delete Method",
      "default": "clear",
      "description": "For DELETE operations: 'clear' preserves row structure, 'remove_rows' shifts data up",
      "human_parameter_name": "Delete method",
      "human_parameter_description": "Choose how you want to delete data. 'Clear' removes the content but keeps the structure, while 'remove_rows' deletes rows and shifts the remaining data up."
    },
    "spreadsheet_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Spreadsheet Id",
      "examples": [
        "1BxiMVs0XRA5nFMdKvBdBZjgmUUqptlbs74OgvE2upms"
      ],
      "description": "The unique alphanumeric ID of the Google Spreadsheet extracted from the URL. Format: A long string of letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores (typically 44 characters). Find it in the URL: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/{SPREADSHEET_ID}/edit. Must be a valid ID - values like 'auto' are NOT valid and will fail.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Google Sheets ID",
      "human_parameter_description": "Provide the unique ID of the Google Spreadsheet you want to work with. This is NOT 'auto' or any placeholder - it must be the actual ID from the spreadsheet URL. Example URL: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1BxiMVs0XRA5nFMdKvBdBZjgmUUqptlbs74OgvE2upms/edit - the ID is '1BxiMVs0XRA5nFMdKvBdBZjgmUUqptlbs74OgvE2upms'."
    }
  }
}
```

## GOOGLESHEETS_FIND_REPLACE
Tool to find and replace text in a Google Spreadsheet. Use when you need to fix formula errors, update values, or perform bulk text replacements across cells. Common use cases: - Fix #ERROR! cells by replacing with empty string or correct formula - Update old values with new ones across multiple cells - Fix formula references or patterns - Clean up data formatting issues

## GOOGLESHEETS_GET_BATCH_VALUES
DEPRECATED: Use GOOGLESHEETS_BATCH_GET instead. Tool to return one or more ranges of values from a spreadsheet. Use when you need to retrieve data from multiple ranges in a single request.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "BatchGetValuesRequest",
  "required": [
    "spreadsheet_id",
    "ranges"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "ranges": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "title": "Ranges",
      "examples": [
        [
          "Sheet1!A1:B10"
        ],
        [
          "Sheet1!A1:B10",
          "Sheet2!C1:D5"
        ]
      ],
      "minItems": 1,
      "description": "The A1 notation or R1C1 notation of the ranges to retrieve values from. Specify one or more ranges (e.g., ['Sheet1!A1:B10', 'Sheet2!C1:D5']). For sheet names with spaces or special characters, wrap in single quotes (e.g., \"'My Sheet'!A1:B10\")."
    },
    "spreadsheet_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Spreadsheet Id",
      "examples": [
        "1BxiMVs0XRA5nFMdKvBdBZjgmUUqptlbs74OgvE2upms"
      ],
      "description": "The ID of the spreadsheet to retrieve data from. This is the unique identifier found in the spreadsheet URL between '/d/' and '/edit' (e.g., '1BxiMVs0XRA5nFMdKvBdBZjgmUUqptlbs74OgvE2upms')."
    },
    "major_dimension": {
      "enum": [
        "DIMENSION_UNSPECIFIED",
        "ROWS",
        "COLUMNS"
      ],
      "type": "string",
      "title": "MajorDimension",
      "description": "The major dimension for results."
    },
    "value_render_option": {
      "enum": [
        "FORMATTED_VALUE",
        "UNFORMATTED_VALUE",
        "FORMULA"
      ],
      "type": "string",
      "title": "ValueRenderOption",
      "description": "How values should be rendered in the output."
    },
    "date_time_render_option": {
      "enum": [
        "SERIAL_NUMBER",
        "FORMATTED_STRING"
      ],
      "type": "string",
      "title": "DateTimeRenderOption",
      "description": "How dates, times, and durations should be represented in the output."
    }
  }
}

## GOOGLESHEETS_GET_CONDITIONAL_FORMAT_RULES
List conditional formatting rules for each sheet (or a selected sheet) in a normalized, easy-to-edit form. Use when you need to view, audit, or prepare to modify conditional format rules.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "GetConditionalFormatRulesRequest",
  "required": [
    "spreadsheet_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "sheet_id": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Sheet Id",
      "examples": [
        0,
        1534097477
      ],
      "description": "Optional filter: return rules only for the sheet with this exact numeric sheetId. If not provided, returns rules for all sheets. If both sheet_title and sheet_id are provided, sheet_id takes precedence."
    },
    "sheet_title": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Sheet Title",
      "examples": [
        "Sheet1",
        "Sales Data"
      ],
      "description": "Optional filter: return rules only for the sheet with this exact title. If not provided, returns rules for all sheets."
    },
    "spreadsheet_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Spreadsheet Id",
      "examples": [
        "12345abcdefGHIJKLMNOPqrstuvwxyz67890UVWXYZ"
      ],
      "description": "Unique identifier of the Google Spreadsheet, typically found in its URL."
    },
    "exclude_tables_in_banded_ranges": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Exclude Tables In Banded Ranges",
      "description": "True if tables should be excluded in the banded ranges. False if not set."
    }
  }
}
```

## GOOGLESHEETS_GET_DATA_VALIDATION_RULES
Tool to extract data validation rules from a Google Sheets spreadsheet. Use when you need to understand dropdown lists, allowed values, custom formulas, or other validation constraints for cells.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "GetDataValidationRulesRequest",
  "required": [
    "spreadsheetId"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "ranges": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "title": "Ranges",
      "examples": [
        [
          "A1:A100",
          "B1:B100"
        ],
        [
          "Sheet1!A:A"
        ]
      ],
      "description": "Optional list of A1 ranges to scan. If omitted, the entire sheet(s) will be scanned. WARNING: Scanning entire large sheets may be slow.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Ranges",
      "human_parameter_description": "List of A1 notation ranges to scan for validation rules."
    },
    "sheetId": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Sheet Id",
      "examples": [
        0,
        123456
      ],
      "description": "Optional sheet ID to filter by. If omitted, all sheets will be scanned.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Sheet ID",
      "human_parameter_description": "The numeric ID of the specific sheet to scan."
    },
    "sheetTitle": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Sheet Title",
      "examples": [
        "Sheet1",
        "Data"
      ],
      "description": "Optional sheet title to filter by. If omitted, all sheets will be scanned.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Sheet Title",
      "human_parameter_description": "The title of the specific sheet to scan."
    },
    "includeEmpty": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Include Empty",
      "default": false,
      "description": "If true, include cells without validation rules in the output. Default is false.",

    },
    "spreadsheetId": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Spreadsheet Id",

      ],
      "description": "The ID of the spreadsheet to request.",

      "human_parameter_description": "The ID of the spreadsheet."
    }
  }
}

## GOOGLESHEETS_GET_SHEET_NAMES
Lists all worksheet names from a specified Google Spreadsheet (which must exist), useful for discovering sheets before further operations.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "GetSheetNamesRequest",
  "required": [
    "spreadsheet_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "exclude_hidden": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Exclude Hidden",
      "default": false,
      "description": "When True, hidden sheets will be excluded from the results. When False (default), all sheets including hidden ones are returned. Hidden sheets are sheets that have been hidden via the 'Hide sheet' option in Google Sheets UI.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Exclude Hidden Sheets",
      "human_parameter_description": "Whether to exclude hidden sheets from the results."
    },
    "spreadsheet_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Spreadsheet Id",
      "examples": [
        "1qpyC0XzvTcKT6EISywY_7H7D7No1tpxEXAMPLE_ID"
      ],
      "description": "The unique identifier of the Google Spreadsheet (alphanumeric string, typically 44 characters). Extract only the ID portion from URLs - do not include leading/trailing slashes, '/edit' suffixes, query parameters, or URL fragments. From 'https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1qpyC0XzvTcKT6EISywY/edit#gid=0', use only '1qpyC0XzvTcKT6EISywY'.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Spreadsheet ID",
      "human_parameter_description": "The spreadsheet id value."
    }
  }
}

## GOOGLESHEETS_GET_SPREADSHEET_BY_DATA_FILTER
Returns the spreadsheet at the given ID, filtered by the specified data filters. Use this tool when you need to retrieve specific subsets of data from a Google Sheet based on criteria like A1 notation, developer metadata, or grid ranges. Important: This action is designed for filtered data retrieval. While it accepts empty filters and returns full metadata in that case, GOOGLESHEETS_GET_SPREADSHEET_INFO is the recommended action for unfiltered spreadsheet retrieval.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "GetSpreadsheetByDataFilterRequest",
  "required": [
    "spreadsheetId"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "dataFilters": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "object",
        "title": "DataFilter",

## GOOGLESHEETS_GET_SPREADSHEET_INFO
Retrieves comprehensive metadata for a Google Spreadsheet using its ID, excluding cell data.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "GetSpreadsheetInfoRequest",
  "properties": {
    "ranges": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "title": "Ranges",
      "examples": [
        [
          "Sheet1!A1:D5"
        ],
        [
          "Sheet1!A1:B10",
          "Sheet2!C1:E20"
        ]
      ],
      "description": "Optional. The ranges to retrieve from the spreadsheet, specified using A1 notation (e.g., 'Sheet1!A1:D5', 'Sheet2!A1:C4'). Multiple ranges can be requested simultaneously. If not specified, metadata for the entire spreadsheet is returned without grid data.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Ranges",
      "human_parameter_description": "Optional list of specific ranges to retrieve using A1 notation. Leave empty to get full spreadsheet metadata."
    },
    "spreadsheet_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Spreadsheet Id",
      "examples": [
        "1BxiMVs0XRA5nFMdKvBdBZjgmUUqptlbs74OgvE2upms",
        "https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1BxiMVs0XRA5nFMdKvBdBZjgmUUqptlbs74OgvE2upms/edit"
      ],
      "minLength": 1,
      "description": "Required. The Google Sheets spreadsheet ID or full URL. Accepts either the ID alone (e.g., '1BxiMVs0XRA5nFMdKvBdBZjgmUUqptlbs74OgvE2upms') or a full Google Sheets URL (e.g., 'https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1BxiMVs0XRA5nFMdKvBdBZjgmUUqptlbs74OgvE2upms/edit'). The ID will be automatically extracted from URLs. Note: Published/embedded URLs (containing '/d/e/2PACX-...') are not supported.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Spreadsheet ID or URL",
      "human_parameter_description": "The Google Sheets spreadsheet ID or full URL. You can paste the entire URL from your browser and the ID will be extracted automatically. Note: Published/embedded URLs are not supported; use the original spreadsheet URL instead."
    },
    "include_grid_data": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Include Grid Data",
      "examples": [
        true,
        false
      ],
      "description": "Optional. If true, grid data will be returned. This parameter is ignored if a field mask was set in the request. When false or not specified, only metadata is returned without cell values.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Include Grid Data",
      "human_parameter_description": "Set to true to include cell values and grid data in the response. Default is false (metadata only)."
    },
    "exclude_tables_in_banded_ranges": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Exclude Tables In Banded Ranges",
      "examples": [
        true,
        false
      ],
      "description": "Optional. If true, tables within banded ranges will be omitted from the response. Default is false when not specified.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Exclude Tables In Banded Ranges",
      "human_parameter_description": "Set to true to exclude tables that appear in banded ranges. Default is false."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request model for getting spreadsheet information."
}
```

## GOOGLESHEETS_GET_TABLE_SCHEMA
DEPRECATED: Use GOOGLESHEETS_GET_SHEET_NAMES and GOOGLESHEETS_GET_SPREADSHEET_INFO for sheet structure metadata, and GOOGLESHEETS_VALUES_GET for direct range inspection. This action is used to get the schema of a table in a Google Spreadsheet, call this action to get the schema of a table in a spreadsheet BEFORE YOU QUERY THE TABLE. Analyze table structure and infer column names, types, and constraints. Uses statistical analysis of sample data to determine the most likely data type for each column. Call this action after calling the LIST_TABLES action to get the schema of a table in a spreadsheet.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "GetTableSchemaRequest",
  "required": [
    "spreadsheet_id",
    "table_name"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "sheet_name": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Sheet Name",
      "description": "Sheet/tab name if table_name is ambiguous across multiple sheets",
      "human_parameter_name": "Sheet Name",
      "human_parameter_description": "The sheet name value."
    },
    "table_name": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Table Name",
      "examples": [
        "Sales Data",
        "Projections",
        "auto"
      ],
      "description": "Table name from LIST_TABLES response OR the visible Google Sheets tab name (e.g., 'Sales Data', 'Projections'). Use 'auto' to analyze the largest/most prominent table.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Table Name",
      "human_parameter_description": "The table name value."
    },
    "sample_size": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Sample Size",
      "default": 50,
      "maximum": 1000,
      "minimum": 1,
      "description": "Number of rows to sample for type inference",
      "human_parameter_name": "Sample Size",
      "human_parameter_description": "The sample size value."
    },
    "spreadsheet_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Spreadsheet Id",
      "examples": [
        "1BxiMVs0XRA5nFMdKvBdBZjgmUUqptlbs74OgvE2upms"
      ],
      "description": "The unique identifier of the Google Spreadsheet. Must be a valid Google Sheets ID (typically a 44-character alphanumeric string). Do NOT use 'auto' - only 'table_name' supports auto-detection. You can get this ID from the spreadsheet URL or from SEARCH_SPREADSHEETS action.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Google Sheets ID",
      "human_parameter_description": "The unique Google Sheets ID from the spreadsheet URL."
    }
  }
}
```

## GOOGLESHEETS_INSERT_DIMENSION
Tool to insert new rows or columns into a sheet at a specified location. Use when you need to add empty rows or columns within an existing Google Sheet.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "InsertDimensionRequestModel",
  "required": [
    "spreadsheet_id",
    "insert_dimension"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "spreadsheet_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Spreadsheet Id",
      "examples": [
        "abc123spreadsheetId"
      ],
      "description": "The ID of the spreadsheet to update.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Spreadsheet ID",
      "human_parameter_description": "The unique identifier of the Google Spreadsheet where rows or columns will be inserted."
    },
    "response_ranges": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"

## GOOGLESHEETS_LIST_TABLES
DEPRECATED: Use GOOGLESHEETS_GET_SHEET_NAMES for tab discovery and GOOGLESHEETS_GET_SPREADSHEET_INFO for full sheet metadata. This action is used to list all tables in a Google Spreadsheet, call this action to get the list of tables in a spreadsheet. Discover all tables in a Google Spreadsheet by analyzing sheet structure and detecting data patterns. Uses heuristic analysis to find header rows, data boundaries, and table structures.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ListTablesRequest",
  "required": [
    "spreadsheet_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "min_rows": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Min Rows",
      "default": 2,
      "minimum": 1,
      "description": "Minimum number of data rows to consider a valid table",
      "human_parameter_name": "Minimum Rows",
      "human_parameter_description": "The minimum rows value."
    },
    "min_columns": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Min Columns",
      "default": 1,
      "minimum": 1,
      "description": "Minimum number of columns to consider a valid table",
      "human_parameter_name": "Minimum Columns",
      "human_parameter_description": "The minimum columns value."
    },
    "min_confidence": {
      "type": "number",
      "title": "Min Confidence",
      "default": 0.5,
      "maximum": 1,
      "minimum": 0,
      "description": "Minimum confidence score (0.0-1.0) to consider a valid table",
      "human_parameter_name": "Minimum Confidence",
      "human_parameter_description": "The minimum confidence value."
    },
    "spreadsheet_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Spreadsheet Id",
      "examples": [
        "1BxiMVs0XRA5nFMdKvBdBZjgmUUqptlbs74OgvE2upms"
      ],
      "description": "The actual Google Spreadsheet ID (not a placeholder or spreadsheet name). Find it in the spreadsheet URL: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/{SPREADSHEET_ID}/edit. It is the alphanumeric string between '/d/' and '/edit' (e.g., '1BxiMVs0XRA5nFMdKvBdBZjgmUUqptlbs74OgvE2upms'). IMPORTANT: Do NOT pass the spreadsheet name - only pass the alphanumeric ID from the URL. Do NOT pass template placeholders like '{{spreadsheet_id}}', '<spreadsheet_id>', or 'your-spreadsheet-id-here'.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Spreadsheet ID",
      "human_parameter_description": "The spreadsheet id value."
    }
  }
}

## GOOGLESHEETS_LOOKUP_SPREADSHEET_ROW
Finds the first row in a Google Spreadsheet where a cell's entire content exactly matches the query string, searching within a specified A1 notation range or the first sheet by default.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "LookupSpreadsheetRowRequest",
  "required": [
    "spreadsheet_id",
    "query"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "query": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Query",
      "examples": [
        "John",
        "Completed",
        "ID-12345"
      ],
      "description": "Exact text value to find; matches the entire content of a cell in a row.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Query",
      "human_parameter_description": "Enter the exact text you want to find in the spreadsheet. This is how you specify what information you need to search for."
    },
    "range": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Range",
      "examples": [
        "Sheet1!A1:D5",
        "Sheet1!A:Z",
        "Sheet1!1:1",
        "'Admin tickets'!A:A"
      ],
      "description": "A1 notation range to search within. Supports cell ranges (e.g., 'Sheet1!A1:D5'), column-only ranges (e.g., 'Sheet1!A:Z'), and row-only ranges (e.g., 'Sheet1!1:1'). Defaults to the first sheet if omitted. IMPORTANT: Sheet names with spaces must be single-quoted (e.g., \"'My Sheet'!A1:Z\"). Bare sheet names without ranges (e.g., 'Sheet1') are not supported - always specify a range.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Range",
      "human_parameter_description": "Specify the range of cells in the spreadsheet you want to search. This helps narrow down the area where the query will look for matches."
    },
    "case_sensitive": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Case Sensitive",
      "default": false,
      "description": "If `True`, the query string search is case-sensitive.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Case sensitive search?",
      "human_parameter_description": "Decide if the search should consider letter casing. Set this to 'True' if you want to match text exactly as you type it."
    },
    "spreadsheet_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Spreadsheet Id",
      "examples": [
        "1BiexwqQYjfC_BXy6zDQYJqb6zxzRyP9"
      ],
      "description": "Identifier of the Google Spreadsheet to search.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Spreadsheet ID",
      "human_parameter_description": "Provide the unique identifier for the Google Spreadsheet you're searching through. This helps target the correct document."
    },
    "value_render_option": {
      "enum": [
        "FORMATTED_VALUE",
        "UNFORMATTED_VALUE",
        "FORMULA"
      ],
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Value Render Option",
      "default": "UNFORMATTED_VALUE",
      "description": "How cell values are rendered in the returned row data. unformatted: raw values without display formatting \u2014 dates appear as serial numbers, e.g. 46009.47 (default, keeps consistency with UPSERT). formatted: display-formatted values \u2014 dates appear as strings, e.g. '2025-12-18'. formula: raw formulas instead of computed values.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Value Render Option",
      "human_parameter_description": "Choose how cell values are returned. Use 'formatted' to get dates as readable strings instead of serial numbers."
    },
    "normalize_whitespace": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Normalize Whitespace",
      "default": true,
      "description": "If `True`, strips leading and trailing whitespace from cell values before matching. This helps match cells like ' TOTAL ' or 'TOTAL ' when searching for 'TOTAL'.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Normalize whitespace?",
      "human_parameter_description": "Decide if whitespace should be stripped from cell values before matching. Recommended to leave True for more robust matching."
    },
    "date_time_render_option": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Date Time Render Option",
      "description": "How dates and times are represented. FORMATTED_STRING: human-readable strings (e.g. '2025-12-18 11:17'). SERIAL_NUMBER: Excel-style serial numbers. Works with all value_render_option settings.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Date Time Render Option",
      "human_parameter_description": "Controls date/time formatting. Use FORMATTED_STRING to get dates like '2025-12-18' instead of '46009.47'."
    }
  }
}

## GOOGLESHEETS_MUTATE_CONDITIONAL_FORMAT_RULES
Add, update, delete, or reorder conditional format rules on a Google Sheet. Use when you need to create, modify, or remove conditional formatting without manually building batchUpdate requests. Supports four operations: ADD (create new rule), UPDATE (replace existing rule), DELETE (remove rule), MOVE (reorder rules by changing index).

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",

                "description": "The start row (inclusive), 0-indexed."
              },
              "endColumnIndex": {

              },
              "startColumnIndex": {

                "title": "Start Column Index",
                "description": "The start column (inclusive), 0-indexed."
              }
            },
            "description": "Range in a sheet where conditional formatting applies."
          },
          "title": "Ranges",
          "description": "Ranges where formatting applies (must be on same sheet)."
        },
        "booleanRule": {
          "type": "object",

                      "type": "boolean",

## GOOGLESHEETS_QUERY_TABLE
DEPRECATED: Use GOOGLESHEETS_VALUES_GET / GOOGLESHEETS_BATCH_GET for table reads and GOOGLESHEETS_LOOKUP_SPREADSHEET_ROW for row lookup/filter workflows. Execute SQL-like SELECT queries against Google Spreadsheet tables. Table names correspond to sheet/tab names visible at the bottom of the spreadsheet. Use GOOGLESHEETS_LIST_TABLES first to discover available table names if unknown. Supports WHERE conditions, ORDER BY, LIMIT clauses.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "QueryTableRequest",
  "required": [
    "spreadsheet_id",
    "sql"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "sql": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Sql",
      "examples": [
        "SELECT * FROM \"Sheet1\" LIMIT 10",
        "SELECT * FROM \"Sales_Data\" LIMIT 10",
        "SELECT project, totals FROM \"Sales_Data\" WHERE totals > 10.0 ORDER BY totals DESC",
        "SELECT name, email FROM \"Customers\" WHERE status = 'ACTIVE'"
      ],
      "description": "SQL SELECT query. The table name is the Google Sheets tab/sheet name (visible at the bottom of the spreadsheet). Use GOOGLESHEETS_LIST_TABLES to discover available table names if unknown. Supported: SELECT cols FROM table WHERE conditions ORDER BY col LIMIT n. Table names must be quoted with double quotes if they contain spaces or are numeric-only (e.g., SELECT * FROM \"My Sheet\" or SELECT * FROM \"415\").",
      "human_parameter_name": "SQL query",
      "human_parameter_description": "The sql query value."
    },
    "spreadsheet_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Spreadsheet Id",
      "examples": [
        "1BxiMVs0XRA5nFMdKvBdBZjgmUUqptlbs74OgvE2upms"
      ],
      "description": "The unique identifier of a native Google Sheets file. Found in the spreadsheet URL after /d/ (e.g., '1BxiMVs0XRA5nFMdKvBdBZjgmUUqptlbs74OgvE2upms'). Only native Google Sheets files (MIME type: application/vnd.google-apps.spreadsheet) are supported. Files uploaded to Google Drive that are not native Google Sheets (such as Excel .xlsx files, PDFs, or Google Docs) will not work even if they can be viewed in Google Sheets.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Google Sheets ID",
      "human_parameter_description": "The unique identifier of a Google Spreadsheet from its URL."
    },
    "include_formulas": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Include Formulas",
      "default": false,
      "description": "Whether to return formula text instead of calculated values for formula columns",
      "human_parameter_name": "Return formula text?",
      "human_parameter_description": "The return formula text? value."
    }
  }
}
```

## GOOGLESHEETS_SEARCH_DEVELOPER_METADATA
Tool to search for developer metadata in a spreadsheet. Use when you need to find specific metadata entries based on filters.

## GOOGLESHEETS_SEARCH_SPREADSHEETS
Search for Google Spreadsheets using various filters including name, content, date ranges, and more.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "SearchSpreadsheetsRequest",
  "properties": {
    "query": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Query",
      "examples": [
        "Budget Report",
        "quarterly sales",
        "name contains 'Budget'",
        "fullText contains 'sales data'",
        "sharedWithMe = true"
      ],
      "description": "Search query to filter spreadsheets. Behavior depends on the 'search_type' parameter. For advanced searches, use Google Drive query syntax with fields like 'name contains', 'fullText contains', or boolean filters like 'sharedWithMe = true'. DO NOT use spreadsheet IDs as search terms. Leave empty to get all spreadsheets.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Query",
      "human_parameter_description": "Search query to filter spreadsheets."
    },
    "order_by": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Order By",
      "default": "modifiedTime desc",
      "description": "Sort order (comma-separated list for multi-field sorting). Valid fields: createdTime, folder, modifiedByMeTime, modifiedTime, name, name_natural, quotaBytesUsed, recency, sharedWithMeTime, starred, viewedByMeTime. Append ' desc' for descending order (default is ascending). Examples: 'modifiedTime desc', 'folder,name', 'starred,modifiedTime desc'.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Order By",
      "human_parameter_description": "Sort order for results."
    },
    "page_token": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Page Token",
      "description": "Token for retrieving the next page of results. Use the 'next_page_token' value from a previous response to get subsequent pages. Leave empty to get the first page.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Page Token",
      "human_parameter_description": "Token for retrieving the next page of results from a previous search."
    },
    "max_results": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Max Results",
      "default": 10,
      "maximum": 1000,
      "minimum": 1,
      "description": "Maximum number of spreadsheets to return (1-1000). Defaults to 10.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Max Results",
      "human_parameter_description": "Maximum number of spreadsheets to return (1-1000). Defaults to 10."
    },
    "search_type": {
      "enum": [
        "name",
        "content",
        "both"
      ],
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Search Type",
      "default": "name",
      "description": "How to search: 'name' searches filenames only (prefix matching from the START of filenames), 'content' uses fullText search which searches file content, name, description, and metadata (Google Drive API limitation: cannot search content exclusively without also matching filenames), 'both' explicitly searches both name OR content with an OR condition. Note: 'name' search only matches from the START of filenames (e.g., 'Budget' finds 'Budget 2024' but NOT 'Q1 Budget').",
      "human_parameter_name": "Search Type",
      "human_parameter_description": "How to search: 'name' for filenames, 'content' for file content/metadata, 'both' for either."
    },
    "starred_only": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Starred Only",
      "default": false,
      "description": "Whether to return only starred spreadsheets. Defaults to False.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Starred Only",
      "human_parameter_description": "Whether to return only starred spreadsheets. Defaults to False."
    },
    "created_after": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Created After",
      "examples": [
        "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z",
        "2024-12-01T12:00:00-08:00"
      ],
      "description": "Return spreadsheets created after this date. Use RFC 3339 format like '2024-01-01T00:00:00Z'.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Created After",
      "human_parameter_description": "Return spreadsheets created after this date. Use RFC 3339 format like"
    },
    "modified_after": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Modified After",
      "examples": [
        "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z",
        "2024-12-01T12:00:00-08:00"
      ],
      "description": "Return spreadsheets modified after this date. Use RFC 3339 format like '2024-01-01T00:00:00Z'.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Modified After",
      "human_parameter_description": "Return spreadsheets modified after this date. Use RFC 3339 format like"
