Tool to set or clear data validation rules (including dropdowns) on a range in Google Sheets. Use when you need to apply dropdown lists, range-based dropdowns, or custom formula validation to cells.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "SetDataValidationRuleRequest",
  "required": [
    "spreadsheet_id",
    "sheet_id",
    "mode",
    "start_row_index",
    "end_row_index",
    "start_column_index",
    "end_column_index"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "mode": {
      "enum": [
        "SET",
        "CLEAR"
      ],
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Mode",
      "examples": [
        "SET",
        "CLEAR"
      ],
      "description": "Operation mode: 'SET' applies a validation rule to the range, 'CLEAR' removes any existing validation from the range."
    },
    "strict": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Strict",
      "default": true,
      "examples": [
        true,
        false
      ],
      "description": "Whether to reject invalid data (true) or show a warning (false). Default is true."
    },
    "values": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "title": "Values",
      "examples": [
        [
          "Option 1",
          "Option 2",
          "Option 3"
        ],
        [
          "Yes",
          "No",
          "Maybe"
        ]
      ],
      "description": "List of allowed values for dropdown. Required when validation_type='ONE_OF_LIST'. Each item becomes a dropdown option."
    },
    "formula": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Formula",
      "examples": [
        "=A1>10",
        "=LEN(A1)<=100",
        "=COUNTIF(A:A,A1)=1"
      ],
      "description": "Custom formula for validation. Required when validation_type='CUSTOM_FORMULA'. Formula should evaluate to TRUE/FALSE. Example: '=A1>10'."
    },
    "sheet_id": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Sheet Id",
      "examples": [
        0,
        1534097477
      ],
      "description": "The unique sheet ID (numeric identifier) where the validation rule will be applied. The first sheet created in a spreadsheet typically has ID 0, while additional sheets get unique IDs (e.g., 1534097477). If a sheet is deleted, its ID is never reused - so if the original first sheet (ID 0) was deleted, attempting to use 0 will fail. Always verify the actual sheet ID exists using GOOGLESHEETS_GET_SPREADSHEET_INFO action (check 'sheets[].properties.sheetId' field)."
    },
    "end_row_index": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "End Row Index",
      "examples": [
        1,
        10
      ],
      "description": "Ending row index (0-based, exclusive) for the validation range. To apply to row 1 only, use start_row_index=0 and end_row_index=1."
    },
    "input_message": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Input Message",
      "examples": [
        "Please select a valid option",
        "Enter a value greater than 10"
      ],
      "description": "Optional message shown to the user when they select the cell. Helpful hint about what values are expected."
    },
    "show_custom_ui": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Show Custom Ui",
      "default": true,
      "examples": [
        true,
        false
      ],
      "description": "Whether to show a dropdown UI for list-based validation. Default is true. Set to true for dropdown lists."
    },
    "spreadsheet_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Spreadsheet Id",
      "examples": [
        "1BxiMVs0XRA5nFMdKvBdBZjgmUUqptlbs74OgvE2upms"
      ],
      "description": "The unique identifier of the Google Sheets spreadsheet. Can be found in the spreadsheet URL between '/d/' and '/edit'."
    },
    "source_range_a1": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Source Range A1",
      "examples": [
        "Sheet1!A1:A10",
        "A1:A5"
      ],
      "description": "Source range in A1 notation for dropdown values. Required when validation_type='ONE_OF_RANGE'. Example: 'Sheet1!A1:A10' or 'A1:A10'."
    },
    "start_row_index": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Start Row Index",
      "examples": [
        0,
        5
      ],
      "description": "Starting row index (0-based, inclusive) for the validation range. Row 1 is index 0."
    },
    "validation_type": {
      "enum": [
        "ONE_OF_LIST",
        "ONE_OF_RANGE",
        "CUSTOM_FORMULA",
        "NUMBER_GREATER",
        "NUMBER_GREATER_THAN_EQ",
        "NUMBER_LESS",
        "NUMBER_LESS_THAN_EQ",
        "NUMBER_EQ",
        "NUMBER_NOT_EQ",
        "NUMBER_BETWEEN",
        "NUMBER_NOT_BETWEEN",
        "TEXT_CONTAINS",
        "TEXT_NOT_CONTAINS",
        "TEXT_EQ",
        "TEXT_NOT_EQ",
        "TEXT_IS_EMAIL",
        "TEXT_IS_URL",
        "DATE_EQ",
        "DATE_BEFORE",
        "DATE_AFTER",
        "DATE_ON_OR_BEFORE",
        "DATE_ON_OR_AFTER",
        "DATE_BETWEEN",
        "DATE_NOT_BETWEEN",
        "DATE_NOT_EQ",
        "DATE_IS_VALID",
        "BLANK",
        "NOT_BLANK",
        "BOOLEAN"
      ],
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Validation Type",
      "examples": [
        "ONE_OF_LIST",
        "NUMBER_GREATER",
        "TEXT_CONTAINS",
        "DATE_BEFORE"
      ],
      "description": "Type of validation rule to apply. Required when mode='SET'. Dropdown types: 'ONE_OF_LIST' (dropdown from list), 'ONE_OF_RANGE' (dropdown from range). Number validations: 'NUMBER_GREATER', 'NUMBER_GREATER_THAN_EQ', 'NUMBER_LESS', 'NUMBER_LESS_THAN_EQ', 'NUMBER_EQ', 'NUMBER_NOT_EQ', 'NUMBER_BETWEEN', 'NUMBER_NOT_BETWEEN'. Text validations: 'TEXT_CONTAINS', 'TEXT_NOT_CONTAINS', 'TEXT_EQ', 'TEXT_NOT_EQ', 'TEXT_IS_EMAIL', 'TEXT_IS_URL' (Note: TEXT_STARTS_WITH and TEXT_ENDS_WITH are only for conditional formatting, not data validation). Date validations: 'DATE_EQ', 'DATE_BEFORE', 'DATE_AFTER', 'DATE_ON_OR_BEFORE', 'DATE_ON_OR_AFTER', 'DATE_BETWEEN', 'DATE_NOT_BETWEEN', 'DATE_NOT_EQ', 'DATE_IS_VALID'. Other: 'BLANK', 'NOT_BLANK', 'BOOLEAN', 'CUSTOM_FORMULA'."
    },
    "condition_values": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "title": "Condition Values",
      "examples": [
        [
          "100"
        ],
        [
          "10",
          "50"
        ],
        [
          "@example.com"
        ]
      ],
      "description": "Generic list of condition values for validation types that require specific values (e.g., NUMBER_GREATER requires one value, NUMBER_BETWEEN requires two values, TEXT_CONTAINS requires one value). For simple validations like TEXT_IS_EMAIL, BLANK, NOT_BLANK, BOOLEAN, DATE_IS_VALID, this can be omitted. Each value should be a string that will be parsed by Google Sheets."
    },
    "end_column_index": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "End Column Index",
      "examples": [
        1,
        5
      ],
      "description": "Ending column index (0-based, exclusive) for the validation range. To apply to column A only, use start_column_index=0 and end_column_index=1."
    },
    "start_column_index": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Start Column Index",
      "examples": [
        0,
        2
      ],
      "description": "Starting column index (0-based, inclusive) for the validation range. Column A is index 0."
    },
    "filtered_rows_included": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Filtered Rows Included",
      "default": false,
      "examples": [
        true,
        false
      ],
      "description": "Whether to apply validation to rows hidden by filters. Default is false. Set to true to ensure validation applies to both visible and filtered rows."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request to set or clear data validation rules on a range in a Google Sheet."
}
```

## GOOGLESHEETS_SHEET_FROM_JSON
DEPRECATED: Use GOOGLESHEETS_CREATE_GOOGLE_SHEET1 + GOOGLESHEETS_UPDATE_VALUES_BATCH (or GOOGLESHEETS_VALUES_UPDATE / GOOGLESHEETS_SPREADSHEETS_VALUES_APPEND) instead. Creates a new Google Spreadsheet and populates its first worksheet from `sheet_json`. When data is provided, the first item's keys establish the headers. An empty list creates an empty worksheet.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "SheetFromJsonRequest",
  "required": [
    "title",
    "sheet_name",
    "sheet_json"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "title": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Title",
      "examples": [
        "Q3 Sales Report",
        "Project Plan Alpha"
      ],
      "description": "The desired title for the new Google Spreadsheet.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Spreadsheet title",
      "human_parameter_description": "The title you want to give your new spreadsheet. This helps identify its purpose easily."
    },
    "sheet_json": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "object",
        "additionalProperties": true
      },
      "title": "Sheet Json",
      "examples": [
        "[{\"Name\": \"Alice\", \"Age\": 30, \"City\": \"New York\"}, {\"Name\": \"Bob\", \"Age\": 24, \"City\": \"London\"}]",
        "[{\"Product ID\": \"A123\", \"Quantity\": 10, \"Price\": 25.50}, {\"Product ID\": \"B456\", \"Quantity\": 5, \"Price\": 100.00}]",
        "[]"
      ],
      "description": "A list of dictionaries representing the rows of the sheet. Each dictionary must have the same set of keys, which will form the header row. Values can be strings, numbers, booleans, or null (represented as empty cells). An empty list [] is allowed and will create a spreadsheet with an empty worksheet.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Sheet data in JSON format",
      "human_parameter_description": "Provide the data for your spreadsheet as a list of rows in JSON format. Make sure each row has the same set of keys for proper formatting. An empty list is allowed and will create an empty spreadsheet."
    },
    "sheet_name": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Sheet Name",
      "examples": [
        "Sheet1",
        "Data Summary",
        "October Metrics"
      ],
      "description": "The name for the first worksheet within the newly created spreadsheet. This name will appear as a tab at the bottom of the sheet.",
      "human_parameter_name": "First worksheet name",
      "human_parameter_description": "The name for the first tab in your spreadsheet. Choose a name that describes the data it will hold."
    }
  }
}
```

## GOOGLESHEETS_SPREADSHEETS_SHEETS_COPY_TO
Tool to copy a single sheet from a spreadsheet to another spreadsheet. Use when you need to duplicate a sheet into a different spreadsheet.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "SpreadsheetsSheetsCopyToRequest",
  "required": [
    "spreadsheet_id",
    "sheet_id",
    "destination_spreadsheet_id"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "sheet_id": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Sheet Id",
      "examples": [
        0
      ],
      "description": "The ID of the sheet to copy.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Sheet Id",
      "human_parameter_description": "The ID of the sheet to copy."
    },
    "spreadsheet_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Spreadsheet Id",
      "examples": [
        "1qZ_..."
      ],
      "description": "The ID of the spreadsheet containing the sheet to copy.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Spreadsheet Id",
      "human_parameter_description": "The ID of the spreadsheet containing the sheet to copy."
    },
    "destination_spreadsheet_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Destination Spreadsheet Id",
      "examples": [
        "2rY_..."
      ],
      "description": "The ID of the spreadsheet to copy the sheet to.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Destination Spreadsheet Id",
      "human_parameter_description": "The ID of the spreadsheet to copy the sheet to."
    }
  }
}

Tool to append values to a spreadsheet. Use when you need to add new data to the end of an existing table in a Google Sheet.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",

Per Google Sheets API documentation, sheet names with spaces or special characters require single quotes (e.g., \"'Email Summary'!A:E\", \"'Jon's Data'!A1:D5\"). Sheet names without spaces/special characters don't need quotes (e.g., 'Sheet1!A:D'). You can provide ranges with or without quotes\u2014the action will add them automatically when needed. The sheet name must exist in the spreadsheet; a non-existent sheet will cause an 'Unable to parse range' error. Check updates.updatedRange in the response for where values were written.",

## GOOGLESHEETS_SPREADSHEETS_VALUES_BATCH_CLEAR
Tool to clear one or more ranges of values from a spreadsheet. Use when you need to remove data from specific cells or ranges while keeping formatting and other properties intact.

**Input schema:**
```json

  "type": "object",

## GOOGLESHEETS_UPDATE_DIMENSION_PROPERTIES
Tool to hide/unhide rows or columns and set row heights or column widths. Use when you need to change visibility or pixel sizing of dimensions in a Google Sheet.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "UpdateDimensionPropertiesRequest",
  "required": [
    "spreadsheet_id",
    "dimension",
    "start_index",
    "end_index"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "sheet_id": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Sheet Id",
      "examples": [
        0,
        123456789
      ],
      "description": "The numeric ID of the sheet (tab). Either sheet_id or sheet_name must be provided. If both are provided, sheet_name will be resolved to sheet_id and override this value."
    },
    "dimension": {
      "enum": [
        "ROWS",
        "COLUMNS"
      ],
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Dimension",
      "examples": [
        "ROWS",
        "COLUMNS"
      ],
      "description": "Whether to update rows or columns."
    },
    "end_index": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "End Index",
      "examples": [
        1,
        10,
        20
      ],
      "description": "The zero-based end index (exclusive) of the dimension range to update. For example, to update rows 5-9, use start_index=5 and end_index=10.",
      "exclusiveMinimum": 0
    },
    "pixel_size": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Pixel Size",
      "examples": [
        100,
        150,
        200
      ],
      "description": "The height (for rows) or width (for columns) in pixels. Must be a positive integer. At least one of hidden_by_user or pixel_size must be provided.",
      "exclusiveMinimum": 0
    },
    "sheet_name": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Sheet Name",
      "examples": [
        "Sheet1",
        "Sales Data"
      ],
      "description": "The name of the sheet (tab). If provided, this will be resolved to the numeric sheet_id using GOOGLESHEETS_GET_SPREADSHEET_INFO. Either sheet_id or sheet_name must be provided."
    },
    "start_index": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Start Index",
      "minimum": 0,
      "examples": [
        0,
        5,
        10
      ],
      "description": "The zero-based start index (inclusive) of the dimension range to update. For rows, 0 is the first row; for columns, 0 is column A."
    },
    "hidden_by_user": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Hidden By User",
      "examples": [
        true,
        false
      ],
      "description": "Whether to hide (true) or unhide (false) the specified rows/columns. At least one of hidden_by_user or pixel_size must be provided."

    "spreadsheet_id": {

      ],

    "response_ranges": {

        "type": "string"
      },
      "title": "Response Ranges",
      "examples": [
        [
          "Sheet1!A1:B10"
        ]
      ],
      "description": "Limits the ranges included in the response spreadsheet (only if includeSpreadsheetInResponse is true)."
    },
    "response_include_grid_data": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Response Include Grid Data",
      "examples": [
        false
      ],
      "description": "Whether to include grid data in the response (only if includeSpreadsheetInResponse is true)."
    },
    "include_spreadsheet_in_response": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Include Spreadsheet In Response",
      "examples": [
        false
      ],
      "description": "Whether to include the updated spreadsheet in the response."
    }
  },
  "description": "Request to update dimension properties via batchUpdate wrapper."
}

## GOOGLESHEETS_UPDATE_SPREADSHEET_PROPERTIES
Tool to update SPREADSHEET-LEVEL properties such as the spreadsheet's title, locale, time zone, or auto-recalculation settings. Use when you need to modify the overall configuration of a Google Spreadsheet. NOTE: To update individual SHEET properties (like renaming a specific sheet/tab), use GOOGLESHEETS_UPDATE_SHEET_PROPERTIES instead.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "UpdateSpreadsheetPropertiesRequestModel",
  "required": [
    "spreadsheetId",

## GOOGLESHEETS_UPDATE_VALUES_BATCH
Tool to set values in one or more ranges of a spreadsheet. Use when you need to update multiple ranges in a single operation for better performance.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "BatchUpdateValuesRequest",
  "required": [
    "spreadsheet_id",
    "valueInputOption",
    "data"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "data": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {

            "title": "Range",
            "examples": [

            "description": "The A1 notation of the range to update (e.g., 'Sheet1!A1:B2', 'Sheet1!C:C', or 'A1:D5'). The range must specify which cells to update."
          },
          "values": {
            "type": "array",
            "items": {
              "type": "array",
              "items": {
                "anyOf": [
                  {
                    "type": "string"

                  {
                    "type": "integer"
                  },
                  {
                    "type": "number"
                  },
                  {
                    "type": "boolean"
                  },
                  {
                    "type": "null"
                  }
                ]
              }
            },
            "title": "Values",
            "examples": [

                  "Name",
                  "Score"
                ],
                [
                  "Alice",
                  "95"
                ]
              ]
            ],
            "description": "The data to write. This is an array of arrays, the outer array representing all the data and each inner array representing a major dimension. Each item in the inner array corresponds with one cell. Supports string, number, boolean, and null values."
          },

            "enum": [

      "title": "Data",

      "pattern": "^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$",
      "examples": [

      ],
      "description": "The ID of the spreadsheet to update. This ID can be found in the URL of the spreadsheet (e.g., https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/{spreadsheet_id}/edit). Must be a valid Google Sheets spreadsheet ID."
    },
    "valueInputOption": {
      "enum": [
        "INPUT_VALUE_OPTION_UNSPECIFIED",
        "RAW",
        "USER_ENTERED"
      ],
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Value Input Option",
      "examples": [
        "USER_ENTERED"
      ],
      "description": "How the input data should be interpreted. RAW: Values are stored exactly as entered, without parsing. USER_ENTERED: Values are parsed as if typed by a user (numbers stay numbers, strings prefixed with '=' become formulas, etc.). INPUT_VALUE_OPTION_UNSPECIFIED: Default input value option is not specified."
    },
    "includeValuesInResponse": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Include Values In Response",
      "examples": [
        false
      ],
      "description": "Determines if the update response should include the values of the cells that were updated. By default, responses do not include the updated values."
    },
    "responseValueRenderOption": {
      "enum": [
        "FORMATTED_VALUE",
        "UNFORMATTED_VALUE",

      "title": "Response Value Render Option",
      "examples": [

      "description": "Determines how values in the response should be rendered. Only used if includeValuesInResponse is true. FORMATTED_VALUE (default): Values are formatted as displayed in the UI. UNFORMATTED_VALUE: Values are unformatted. FORMULA: Formulas are not evaluated."

  }

## GOOGLESHEETS_UPSERT_ROWS
Upsert rows - update existing rows by key, append new ones. Automatically handles column mapping and partial updates. Use for: CRM syncs (match Lead ID), transaction imports (match Transaction ID), inventory updates (match SKU), calendar syncs (match Event ID). Features: - Auto-adds missing columns to sheet - Partial column updates (only update Phone + Status, preserve other columns) - Column order doesn't matter (auto-maps by header name) - Prevents duplicates by matching key column Example inputs: - Contact update: keyColumn='Email', headers=['Email','Phone','Status'], data=[['john@ex.com','555-0101','Active']] - Inventory sync: keyColumn='SKU', headers=['SKU','Stock','Price'], data=[['WIDGET-001',50,9.99],['GADGET-002',30,19.99]] - CRM lead update: keyColumn='Lead ID', headers=['Lead ID','Score','Status'], data=[['L-12345',85,'Hot']] - Partial update: keyColumn='Email', headers=['Email','Phone'] (only updates Phone, preserves Name/Address/etc)

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "UpsertRowsRequest",
  "required": [
    "spreadsheetId",
    "sheetName",
    "rows"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "rows": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "array",
        "items": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "type": "string"
            },
            {
              "type": "integer"
            },
            {
              "type": "number"
            },
            {
              "type": "boolean"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ]
        }
      },
      "title": "Rows",
      "examples": [
        [
          [
            "john@example.com",
            "555-0101",
            "Active"
          ],
          [
            "jane@example.com",
            "555-0102",
            "Pending"
          ]
        ],
        [
          [
            "WIDGET-001",
            50,
            9.99
          ],
          [
            "GADGET-002",
            30,
            19.99
          ]
        ],
        [
          [
            "L-12345",
            "John Doe",
            85
          ]
        ]
      ],
      "minItems": 1,
      "description": "2D array of data rows to upsert. IMPORTANT: If 'headers' is NOT provided, the FIRST row is treated as column headers and remaining rows as data - so you need at least 2 rows (1 header + 1 data). If 'headers' IS provided separately, then ALL rows in this array are treated as data rows. Each row should have the same number of values as headers. If a row has MORE values than headers: with strict_mode=true (default), an error is returned showing which rows are affected; with strict_mode=false, extra values are silently truncated. If a row has FEWER values than headers, an error is returned during execution. Cell values can be strings, numbers, booleans, or null. Example with headers provided: headers=['Email','Status'], rows=[['john@ex.com','Active']] (1 data row). Example without headers: rows=[['Email','Status'],['john@ex.com','Active']] (row 1 = headers, row 2 = data).",
      "human_parameter_name": "Data",
      "human_parameter_description": "Enter the actual data rows you want to insert or update. Ensure each row matches the provided headers."
    },
    "headers": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "title": "Headers",
      "examples": [
        [
          "Email",
          "Phone",
          "Status"
        ],
        [
          "Lead ID",
          "Name",
          "Score"
        ],
        [
          "SKU",
          "Stock",
          "Price"
        ]
      ],
      "description": "List of column names for the data. These will be matched against sheet headers. If a column doesn't exist in the sheet, it will be added automatically. Order doesn't need to match sheet order. Can be auto-derived from the first row in 'rows' if not provided. Example inputs: ['Email', 'Phone', 'Status'] for contact updates, ['Lead ID', 'Name', 'Score'] for CRM, ['SKU', 'Stock', 'Price'] for inventory.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Headers",
      "human_parameter_description": "Provide the names of the columns you want to upsert data for. They should match the existing headers in the sheet."
    },
    "keyColumn": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Key Column",
      "examples": [
        "Email",
        "ID",
        "SKU",
        "Lead ID",
        "Transaction Number"
      ],
      "description": "The column NAME (header text) to use as unique identifier for matching rows. Must be an actual header name from the sheet (e.g., 'Email', 'Lead ID', 'SKU'), NOT a column letter (e.g., 'A', 'B', 'C'). If you provide a column letter like 'A', it will be automatically converted to the header name at that column position. If neither 'key_column' nor 'key_column_index' is provided, defaults to the first column (index 0).",
      "human_parameter_name": "Key Column",
      "human_parameter_description": "Specify the name of the column that contains unique identifiers to match existing rows."
    },
    "sheetName": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Sheet Name",
      "examples": [
        "Leads",
        "Transactions",
        "Inventory",
        "Sheet1",
        "\u5de5\u4f5c\u88681"
      ],
      "description": "The name of the sheet/tab within the spreadsheet. Note: Google Sheets creates default sheets with localized names based on account language (e.g., 'Sheet1' for English, '\u5de5\u4f5c\u88681' for Chinese, 'Hoja1' for Spanish, 'Feuille1' for French, 'Planilha1' for Portuguese, '\u041b\u0438\u0441\u04421' for Russian). If you specify a common default name and the sheet is not found, the action will automatically use the first sheet if only one exists.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Sheet Name",
      "human_parameter_description": "Enter the name of the sheet you want to update within the spreadsheet."
    },
    "strictMode": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Strict Mode",
      "default": true,
      "description": "Controls how rows with mismatched column counts are handled. When True (default), an error is returned if any row has more values than headers - the error message shows exactly which rows are affected and what values would need to be removed. When False, extra values are silently truncated to match the header count. Set to False only if you explicitly want automatic truncation of extra values.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Strict Mode",
      "human_parameter_description": "When enabled (default), rejects rows with extra values. Disable to auto-truncate extra values."
    },
    "tableStart": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Table Start",
      "default": "A1",
      "examples": [
        "A1",
        "C5",
        "D10"
      ],
      "description": "Cell where the table starts (where headers are located). Defaults to 'A1'. Use this if your table is offset (e.g., 'C5', 'D10').",
      "human_parameter_name": "Table Start",
      "human_parameter_description": "Specify the cell where your data headers start in the sheet, such as 'A1' or 'C5'."
    },
    "spreadsheetId": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Spreadsheet Id",
      "examples": [
        "1BxiMVs0XRA5nFMdKvBdBZjgmUUqptlbs74OgvE2upms"
      ],
      "description": "The ID of the spreadsheet. Must be a non-empty string, typically a 44-character alphanumeric string found in the spreadsheet URL.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Spreadsheet ID",
      "human_parameter_description": "Provide the unique ID of the Google Spreadsheet where you want to upsert rows."
    },
    "key_column_index": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "type": "integer"
        },
        {
          "type": "number"
        }
      ],
      "title": "Key Column Index",
      "examples": [
        0,
        1,
        2
      ],
      "description": "The 0-based column index to use as unique identifier for matching rows. Alternative to 'key_column' - will be converted to column name using headers. If neither 'key_column' nor 'key_column_index' is provided, defaults to 0 (first column). Example: 0 for first column, 1 for second column."
    },
    "normalization_message": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Normalization Message",
      "description": "Internal field to track input normalization (e.g., row truncation). Not part of API."
    }
  },
  "description": "Upsert (update or insert) rows in a Google Sheet based on a key column.\nAutomatically handles column mapping, partial updates, and adds missing columns."
}

## GOOGLESHEETS_VALUES_GET
Returns a range of values from a spreadsheet. Use when you need to read data from specific cells or ranges in a Google Sheet.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ValuesGetRequest",
  "required": [
    "spreadsheet_id",
    "range"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "range": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Range",
      "examples": [
        "Sheet1!A1:B3",
        "'My Sheet'!A1:D5",
        "'Feuille 1'!A1:C10",
        "A1:D5",
        "Sheet1!A:A"
      ],
      "description": "The A1 notation or R1C1 notation of the range to retrieve values from. If the sheet name contains spaces or special characters, wrap the sheet name in single quotes (e.g., \"'My Sheet'!A1:B2\"). Without single quotes, the API will return a 400 error for sheet names with spaces. Examples: 'Sheet1!A1:B3', \"'Sheet With Spaces'!A1:D5\", 'A1:D5' (no sheet name uses first visible sheet), 'Sheet1!A:A' (entire column), 'SheetName' (entire sheet).",
      "human_parameter_name": "Range",
      "human_parameter_description": "Specify the range of cells you want to retrieve using A1 notation (e.g., 'A1:B10', 'Sheet1!A1:C5'). If the sheet name contains spaces or special characters, enclose the sheet name in single quotes (e.g., \"'My Sheet'!A1:B2\")."
    },
    "end_row": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "End Row",
      "description": "1-based row number to stop reading at (inclusive). Use with start_row for pagination to avoid large response errors. Example: start_row=501, end_row=1000 fetches rows 501-1000.",
      "human_parameter_name": "End Row",
      "human_parameter_description": "Last row to read (1-based). Leave empty to read to the end of the range."
    },
    "start_row": {
      "type": "integer",
      "title": "Start Row",
      "description": "1-based row number to start reading from (inclusive). Use with end_row for pagination to avoid large response errors. Example: start_row=1, end_row=500 fetches the first 500 rows.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Start Row",
      "human_parameter_description": "First row to read (1-based). Leave empty to start from the beginning of the range."
    },
    "spreadsheet_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Spreadsheet Id",
      "examples": [
        "1BxiMVs0XRA5nFMdKvBdBZjgmUUqptlbs74OgvE2upms",
        "13I9BjRCKl1iy7VZ-_Ir29qr5Yu79iIyIkooVqApymS8"
      ],
      "description": "The unique identifier of the Google Spreadsheet from which to retrieve values. This is the long alphanumeric string found in the spreadsheet URL between '/d/' and '/edit' (e.g., '1BxiMVs0XRA5nFMdKvBdBZjgmUUqptlbs74OgvE2upms'). WARNING: Do NOT use the spreadsheet name or title (e.g., 'My Sales Report'); you must use the actual ID from the URL.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Spreadsheet Id",
      "human_parameter_description": "Provide the unique ID of the spreadsheet you want to extract values from. The ID is the long alphanumeric string in the URL between '/d/' and '/edit'. Do NOT use the spreadsheet name."
    },
    "major_dimension": {
      "enum": [
        "DIMENSION_UNSPECIFIED",
        "ROWS",
        "COLUMNS"
      ],
      "type": "string",
      "title": "MajorDimension",
      "description": "The major dimension for results.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Major Dimension",
      "human_parameter_description": "Indicate whether you want your data organized by rows or columns. If you're not sure, it defaults to rows."
    },
    "value_render_option": {
      "enum": [
        "FORMATTED_VALUE",
        "UNFORMATTED_VALUE",
        "FORMULA"
      ],
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Value Render Option",
      "default": "FORMATTED_VALUE",
      "description": "How values should be rendered in the output. FORMATTED_VALUE: Values are calculated and formatted (default). UNFORMATTED_VALUE: Values are calculated but not formatted. FORMULA: Values are not calculated; the formula is returned instead.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Value Render Option",
      "human_parameter_description": "Choose how you want the values to be displayed. You can get the formatted version, an unformatted version, or just the underlying formula."
    },
    "date_time_render_option": {
      "enum": [
        "SERIAL_NUMBER",
        "FORMATTED_STRING"
      ],
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Date Time Render Option",
      "default": "SERIAL_NUMBER",
      "description": "How dates, times, and durations should be represented in the output. SERIAL_NUMBER: Dates are returned as serial numbers (default). FORMATTED_STRING: Dates returned as formatted strings.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Date Time Render Option",
      "human_parameter_description": "Select how you want dates and times to be shown. You can use serial numbers or get formatted strings."
    }
  }
}

## GOOGLESHEETS_VALUES_UPDATE
Tool to set values in a range of a Google Spreadsheet. Use when you need to update or overwrite existing cell values in a specific range.

**Input schema:**
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "ValuesUpdateRequest",
  "required": [
    "spreadsheet_id",
    "range",
    "value_input_option",
    "values"
  ],
  "properties": {
    "range": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Range",
      "examples": [
        "Sheet1!A1:C2",
        "Sheet2!B3:F10",
        "A1:Z100"
      ],
      "description": "The A1 notation of the range to update values in (e.g., 'Sheet1!A1:C2', 'MySheet!C:C', or 'A1:D5'). Must be actual cell references, not placeholder values. If the sheet name is omitted (e.g., 'A1:B2'), the operation applies to the first visible sheet. IMPORTANT: The range must not exceed the sheet's grid dimensions. By default, new sheets have 1000 rows and 26 columns (A-Z). If you need to write to columns beyond Z (e.g., AA, AB), first expand the sheet using GOOGLESHEETS_APPEND_DIMENSION or check the current dimensions using GOOGLESHEETS_GET_SPREADSHEET_INFO.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Range",
      "human_parameter_description": "Specify the exact range in the spreadsheet where you want the values to be updated. Use A1 notation for accuracy. Ensure the range does not exceed the sheet's current grid dimensions."
    },
    "values": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "array",
        "items": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "type": "string"
            },
            {
              "type": "integer"
            },
            {
              "type": "number"
            },
            {
              "type": "boolean"
            }
          ]
        }
      },
      "title": "Values",
      "examples": [
        [
          [
            "Name",
            "Age",
            "City"
          ],
          [
            "Test User",
            "25",
            "San Francisco"
          ]
        ]
      ],
      "description": "The data to write. This is an array of arrays, the outer array representing all the data and each inner array representing a major dimension. Each item in the inner array corresponds with one cell.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Values",
      "human_parameter_description": "Provide the data you want to write into the specified range. This should be structured in arrays to correspond to the layout of the spreadsheet."
    },
    "spreadsheet_id": {
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Spreadsheet Id",
      "examples": [
        "13I9BjRCKl1iy7VZ-_Ir29qr5Yu79iIyIkooVqApymS8"
      ],
      "description": "The unique identifier of the Google Spreadsheet to update. This ID can be found in the URL of the spreadsheet (e.g., https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/{spreadsheet_id}/edit). Must be a non-empty string.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Spreadsheet Id",
      "human_parameter_description": "Provide the unique ID of the spreadsheet you want to update. You can find this ID in the spreadsheet's URL."
    },
    "major_dimension": {
      "enum": [
        "ROWS",
        "COLUMNS"
      ],
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Major Dimension",
      "examples": [
        "ROWS"
      ],
      "description": "The major dimension of the values. ROWS (default) means each inner array is a row of values. COLUMNS means each inner array is a column of values. Defaults to ROWS if unspecified.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Major Dimension",
      "human_parameter_description": "Indicate whether your data is organized by rows or columns. Use ROWS for row-wise data or COLUMNS for column-wise data."
    },
    "auto_expand_sheet": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Auto Expand Sheet",
      "default": true,
      "examples": [
        true
      ],
      "description": "If True (default), automatically expands the sheet's dimensions (adds columns/rows) when the target range exceeds the current grid limits. If False, the operation will fail with an error if the range exceeds grid limits.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Auto-expand sheet",
      "human_parameter_description": "Enable automatic expansion of the sheet when writing beyond current grid limits. Disable to receive an error instead."
    },
    "value_input_option": {
      "enum": [
        "RAW",
        "USER_ENTERED"
      ],
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Value Input Option",
      "examples": [
        "USER_ENTERED",
        "RAW"
      ],
      "description": "How the input data should be interpreted. RAW: Values are stored exactly as entered, without parsing (dates, formulas, etc. remain as strings). USER_ENTERED: Values are parsed as if typed by a user (numbers stay numbers, strings prefixed with '=' become formulas, etc.).",
      "human_parameter_name": "Value Input Option",
      "human_parameter_description": "Choose how the input values should be treated. Select RAW for exact values or USER_ENTERED for automatic parsing like a user would do."
    },
    "include_values_in_response": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "title": "Include Values In Response",
      "examples": [
        false
      ],
      "description": "Determines if the update response should include the values of the cells that were updated. By default, responses do not include the updated values.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Include values in response?",
      "human_parameter_description": "Decide if you want the updated cell values included in the response after the operation."
    },
    "response_value_render_option": {
      "enum": [
        "FORMATTED_VALUE",
        "UNFORMATTED_VALUE",
        "FORMULA"
      ],
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Response Value Render Option",
      "examples": [
        "FORMATTED_VALUE"
      ],
      "description": "Determines how values in the response should be rendered. Only used if includeValuesInResponse is true. FORMATTED_VALUE (default): Values are formatted as displayed in the UI. UNFORMATTED_VALUE: Values are unformatted (numbers, booleans, formulas). FORMULA: Formulas are not evaluated and remain as text.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Response value render option",
      "human_parameter_description": "Specify how you would like the values in the response to be displayed. Choose formatted for a user-friendly view or unformatted for raw values."
    },
    "response_datetime_render_option": {
      "enum": [
        "SERIAL_NUMBER",
        "FORMATTED_STRING"
      ],
      "type": "string",
      "title": "Response Datetime Render Option",
      "examples": [
        "SERIAL_NUMBER"
      ],
      "description": "Determines how dates, times, and durations in the response should be rendered. Only used if includeValuesInResponse is true. SERIAL_NUMBER (default): Dates are returned as numbers. FORMATTED_STRING: Dates are returned as strings formatted per the cell's locale.",
      "human_parameter_name": "Response datetime render option",
      "human_parameter_description": "Indicate how you want dates and times to appear in the response. Choose serial number for numeric representation or formatted string for a more readable format."
    }
  }
}
